newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 20.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Kangwon province governor Choi Gak-kyu, who bolted from splinter opposition party in a surprise move, under investigation for taking bribes from businessmen who want to open casino operation in the province.

- Elected governor of Kangwon province, Choi Gak-kyu, two lawmakers and a mayor, in surprise announcement, bolted from the opposition United Liberal Democratic Party. In an announcement, Choi claimed his affiliation with the opposition party made it hard for him to administer local affairs.
- Partial cabinet reshuffle due today. Five cabinet portfolios likely to be affected.
- Korea Development Institute sees fall in GDP growth to 6.4 percent next year.
- Canadian Prime Minister Chretien to visit South Korea from January 9 to 14.

- Peruvian rebels threatened to kill hostages held at the Japanese Ambassador's residence, while the Canadian, Greek, German ambassadors were freed. Japan vowed to secure safe release of Korean Ambassador Lee Won-young and other hostages.
